items.stem: Complete the statement: An irrecoverable debt is written off by …
options: debiting irrecoverable debts and crediting bank
debiting sales and crediting the customer
debiting irrecoverable debts and crediting the customer's account
debiting the customer and crediting irrecoverable debts
items.answer: debiting irrecoverable debts and crediting the customer's account
items.markingKey: debiting irrecoverable debts and crediting the customer's account. The receivable is removed and the expense recorded [1]

items.stem: Explain why irrecoverable debts are written off rather than left in trade receivables.
items.answer: The amount will never be received, so leaving it would overstate assets and profit; the prudence concept requires the loss to be recognised.
items.markingKey: Will not be received – overstates assets [1]; prudence [1] [2]

items.stem: State two reasons why a debt may become irrecoverable.
items.answer: The customer has become bankrupt or gone into liquidation; the customer has disappeared or disputes the debt and legal action is not worthwhile.
items.markingKey: Any two [1 each] [2]

items.stem: Nile Valley Dairy prepared draft profit of $45,260. These items have not been recorded. Calculate the corrected profit for the year.
items.markingKey: $45,260 − $2,750 irrecoverable debts + $1,370 recovered = $43,880 [2]

items.stem: Distinguish between an irrecoverable debt and a doubtful debt.
items.answer: An irrecoverable debt is known to be uncollectable and is written off; a doubtful debt may not be collected, so an allowance is made but the debt stays in the receivables ledger.
items.markingKey: Irrecoverable – certain, written off [1]; doubtful – uncertain, allowance only [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why only the change in the allowance is recorded in the income statement each year.
items.answer: The existing allowance was charged in earlier years; charging the full amount again would double-count the expense.
items.markingKey: Earlier allowance already charged [1]; avoid double counting [1] [2]
